hook: In 1973, a company you use every week was 24 hours from bankruptcy. It survived on a blackjack table in Las Vegas.

beats.voiceover: In 1973, a company you use every week was twenty-four hours from going under.
beats.visual_cue: Grounded cargo jets parked on a dark tarmac at night, ominous stillness, one dim light

beats.voiceover: It couldn't even pay for the fuel to fly its own planes.
beats.visual_cue: Empty fuel gauge needle on red, idle jet engine in cold hangar

beats.voiceover: There was exactly five thousand dollars left in the bank.
beats.visual_cue: A near-empty bank ledger page, a thin stack of a few bills under a desk lamp

beats.voiceover: And a fuel bill for twenty-four thousand, due Monday morning.
beats.visual_cue: An overdue invoice stamped in dirty red ink, close macro of the total

beats.voiceover: So the founder did something no business school would ever teach.
beats.visual_cue: Silhouette of a man in a suit staring out a high office window at night

beats.voiceover: He took the last five grand,
beats.visual_cue: A hand folding cash into a coat pocket, tense close-up

beats.voiceover: and flew it straight to Las Vegas.
beats.visual_cue: 1970s Las Vegas strip at night, glowing neon signs, wide establishing shot

beats.voiceover: This company was Federal Express. The founder, Fred Smith.
beats.visual_cue: A vintage 1970s cargo plane on a runway, a determined founder in period suit beside it

beats.voiceover: He sat down at the blackjack table and bet everything.
beats.visual_cue: Green blackjack felt, cards and casino chips, a hand pushing the whole stack forward

beats.voiceover: By the end of the weekend, five thousand had become twenty-seven.
beats.visual_cue: A growing pile of casino chips overflowing across the green felt

beats.voiceover: Enough to cover the fuel. The planes flew Monday.
beats.visual_cue: A cargo jet lifting off into a golden dawn sky, hopeful

beats.voiceover: But here's the part nobody tells you.
beats.visual_cue: Tight portrait of the founder's face, half in shadow, contemplative

beats.voiceover: The gamble bought time, not survival.
beats.visual_cue: Calendar pages flipping fast, sand slipping through an hourglass

beats.voiceover: That time let him raise eleven million more, and build a company worth billions.
beats.visual_cue: A rising line chart over a fleet of cargo planes multiplying across the sky

beats.voiceover: One insane bet, because the alternative was zero.
beats.visual_cue: A single casino chip resting on green felt under a spotlight, echoing the opening

cta: Save this for the next time everyone says your plan is too crazy to work.
